matchup_findings.statement: Virginia Tech's defense generates sacks and negative plays against an offense that allows them (-2.85 for Clemson's offense).
Virginia Tech holds the early-down edge: its offense stays ahead of the chains on 1st and 2nd down against this defense (+0.95) more than Clemson does (-1.29).
Virginia Tech's explosive rushing offense meets a Clemson defense that allows explosive rush plays (+2.23).
Virginia Tech's defense out-rates the opposing offense on a down-to-down basis (-1.22 for Clemson's offense).

Virginia Tech owns the stronger opponent-adjusted explosive-play matchup: Clemson offense vs Virginia Tech defense -0.49, Virginia Tech offense vs Clemson defense +0.94 (explosive-play rate, opponent-adjusted: Virginia Tech offense #22 of 138, Clemson defense #80 of 138).

Virginia Tech owns the stronger opponent-adjusted scoring matchup: Clemson offense vs Virginia Tech defense -0.72, Virginia Tech offense vs Clemson defense +0.47 (points per game, opponent-adjusted: Virginia Tech offense #25 of 138, Clemson defense #46 of 138).

Virginia Tech owns the stronger opponent-adjusted sustained-efficiency matchup: Clemson offense vs Virginia Tech defense -1.22, Virginia Tech offense vs Clemson defense +0.29 (success rate, opponent-adjusted: Virginia Tech offense #31 of 138, Clemson defense #47 of 138).
Virginia Tech's sustained-efficiency edge is real but not decisive (1.50, below the 2.0 strong threshold): enough for the trailing side to stay in range.
Clemson's offense has given the ball away at a high rate (+1.39 SD). Regression-prone: reported as volatility, never as a cause on its own.

pace.definition: possession_environment = (z of home offense plays + z of away defense plays allowed + z of away offense plays + z of home defense plays allowed) / 2, on adjusted values. Positive = more snaps than an average FBS game. tempo_environment = -(z of each offense's possession seconds per play) / 2

volatility.definition: offense_ypp_residual_sd = game-to-game spread of the offense's yards per play around what the fit expected against each opponent; its percentile is within the FBS universe. explosive_yard_share_z is the raw share standardised across FBS (not opponent-adjusted). takeaways_per_game_z and giveaways_per_game_z are RAW per-game turnover counts standardised across FBS: turnovers are regression-prone and are deliberately not opponent-adjusted.
